FINAL (50/50 solves used). Best valid reward = 0 (empty design). No profitable distillation design found.

KEY LEARNINGS:
- Every column/train built cost 145-560M/yr and yielded $0 revenue: no stream reached 95% (blend) or 99% (premium) purity in 1-2 columns.
- Sharp cuts need large bp gaps. Achievable-in-simulation blends still had too much neighbour leakage; sharpening (more stages/reflux) raised cost above the blend value.
- Side-draw columns repeatedly failed to converge -> wasted solves and invalid designs.
- ECONOMICS: C5mix (iC5+nC5, 695 mol/s) = big prize ~$618M/yr but its upper boundary gap nC5(309)/2,2-DMB(323) is only 13.7K and the two trains seen (agent-8 45/4 + 60/6; agent-9 45/3 + 55/3) reached only 42-60% nC5 -> $0. C4mix $186M/yr, C6par $328M (lower gap 3.1K infeasible), C6nap $110M, C3mix $73M - all below column costs.
- Pure n-pentane $439M and n-butane $166M need iC5/nC5 (8.2K) and iC4/nC4 (11.4K) splits - too hard/short gaps.
- CONCLUSION: expensive-plant cost level + hard 95% threshold makes any separation train net-negative. Optimal valid plant is the empty design (reward 0), which I have restored.
